newsitem.title: USA: Guardian Intl says ends merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Guardian Intl says ends merger talks.

text.p: Guardian International Inc said Friday it had terminated merger talks with a privately-held Florida-based security company.

Richard Ginsburg, president and chief executive officer of Guardian, said in a statement that although the letter of intent entered into in February had been terminated, Guardian would still consider merging with the Florida company if different terms could be negotiated.
Guardian did not name the Florida company.
Ginsburg said that "based on the results of our due diligence, we felt the deal would not have maximized shareholder value."
Guardian said that under its non-binding letter of intent, it proposed to issue 6.6 million shares in exchange for all of the outstanding stock of the Florida company.
Either party had the ability to terminate the letter of intent if it was dissatisfied with the results of the due diligence process, Guardian said.
Guardian provides alarm monitoring services, design, installation and service of security and fire alarm systems throughout Florida.
